m208 at 10/1 and 100 ul extends the same-loading 0/1 and 2/1 observations a8ad1c1e7d0c3c312f29 and f525413ea8aed78db62a. Prediction 12.65/36.88 mL introduces a large completion rise from the measured 2/1 value of 10.80 mL. This directly tests extrapolation for iodophenol.

m208 at 20/1 and 100 ul pairs with the selected 10/1 row at identical loading. Prediction 23.13/59.81 mL implies continued growth of both endpoints. These labels discriminate a steep phenol-specific response from overtransfer of late-elution behavior learned elsewhere.

Previously unobserved m154, the ortho isomer of trifluoromethoxy aryl iodide m153, is predicted at 5.08/8.97 mL at 1/1 and 100 ul. Measured para-isomer reference 77dcc64e3f31b0758f91 gave 5.75/11.02 mL under corresponding conditions. This establishes an early-elution anchor for a new connectivity with nearly matched sample mass.

m154 at 50/1 and 100 ul pairs with its selected 1/1 anchor. Prediction 6.17/10.90 mL implies a shallow solvent response despite a large change in PE/EA. Measuring both conditions tests whether transfer from the para isomer misses a positional effect and informs the remaining m154 rows.

m153 at 50/1 and 100 ul provides the weak-eluent companion to the selected ortho-isomer row, with sample masses 184 and 185.5 mg respectively. Prediction 6.11/11.57 mL is close to that for m154. This comparison tests whether their predicted similarity survives at weak eluent, while 77dcc64e3f31b0758f91 anchors m153 at 1/1.

m181 lactone at 10/1 and 100 ul is predicted at 14.28/25.12 mL. It fills the solvent-response gap below same-loading observation 10ea0c665f5ba7c91bbf at 20/1, 32.91/52.53 mL. This constrains whether its response has a sharp transition distinct from ordinary ester and ketone curves.

m181 at 50/1 and 150 ul tests the unmeasured weak-eluent branch, predicted at 47.04/78.25 mL. Alongside the selected 10/1 row and measured 10ea0c665f5ba7c91bbf, it extends lactone coverage across a substantial response range. The changed sample amount remains an explicit covariate rather than a pure solvent contrast.

Aliphatic conjugated aldehyde m53 at 50/1 and 100 ul is predicted at 22.28/51.75 mL, beyond its measured moderate-retention 2/1 and 5/1 references 59bbda2fab97a5d45827 and e83cbe662d2235b30b7e. This tests a poorly constrained extrapolation and broadens learning beyond aromatic carbonyls.

m85 at 20/1 and 50 ul fills a large condition gap beyond measured 2/1 anchor c2349adace8ee903700a. Related chloroester observation 812adebe27af25dc2242 provides a family reference, with its different conditions retained.

Methoxybenzophenone m114 at 50/1 and 100 ul is predicted at 24.33/52.69 mL. Same-loading 10/1 observation 5fb70d195002f8a4d518 gave 8.81/24.01 mL. This unmeasured weak-eluent branch can define how far carbonyl corrections should transfer to a conjugated diaryl ketone.

Measured f2931e18ce0362f7a6c0 at 2/1 and 9aaa9e876dd61f679e7d at 5/1 constrain earlier parts of its response, although the latter uses 150 ul. Para-nitrobenzaldehyde m193 at 10/1 and 100 ul is predicted at 27.27/51.54 mL. Measured a5f9179bfb146ad70953 establishes late elution at 20/1 with a different sample amount. This intermediate condition constrains its curve and limits indiscriminate transfer from the ortho-nitroaldehyde series.

Ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde m198 at 50/1 and 100 ul is predicted at 27.53/66.96 mL. Observations e99da719af7e2c3e9a93 and 857ae40d0fdf1c7e387e establish its 10/1 and 20/1 behavior at 150 ul. Measured 1f70add69a6dbecca3b4 at 5/1 with PE loading and a2f83665cfe821271b30 at 10/1 with DCM loading establish substantial condition response. This tests the next weak-eluent branch and whether completion growth is learned for this acid rather than borrowed from ester analogues.

Salicylaldehyde m197 at 50/1 and 50 ul extends same-loading 20/1 observation f6b05afc9acf85dffb0f, 11.13/35.03 mL. Prediction 15.88/50.49 mL tests continued completion growth in a family where measured 70abe1d9543e6cae908e showed a broad interval with relatively early onset.

This tests the predicted modest response when the carbonyl is separated from the aromatic ring by a methylene group.

This tests whether an ether-linked acrylate develops a strong weak-eluent response and helps bound transfer from more strongly retained multi-carbonyl esters.

Same-loading 5/1 observation 05ae46c25f5bd347b3a1 gave 6.16/17.46 mL, while beta-ketoester m81 remains modest at 50/1 in 57646b9484b03f4076bb. hypotheses.content: Some recorded endpoint differences depend jointly on sample loading, loading-solvent volume and solvent strength. The predictor's near-invariance to loading changes may miss these relationships, although discordant observations can also reflect unrecorded experimental variation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched comparisons can separate learnable condition interactions from scaffold offsets and establish where additional labels mainly expose unexplained variation. This is especially relevant to the recent m125 failure.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the completed m125 sample-amount by DCM-volume design show a consistent interaction, and does m207 retain its unusual loading response at both 5/1 and 10/1?

hypotheses.content: Measured m208 and m209 are early through 2/1, while their predicted weaker-eluent curves rise sharply. Whether that extrapolation is warranted, and whether onset and completion rise proportionally, remains unresolved for each phenol.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These scaffolds have many eligible conditions but no measured weak-eluent branch. Their early anchors support the starting regime, not the predicted steep rise. Two local curves can delimit transfer of donor-related corrections.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do constant-loading m209 measurements at 5/1 and 20/1 and m208 measurements at 10/1 and 20/1 confirm the predicted rises or reveal flatter, endpoint-specific responses?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl linkage matters for condition response: measured beta-ketoesters m25 and m82 can develop large completion volumes, whereas aryl beta-ketoester m81 and malonate m80 remain comparatively modest at weak eluent. Transfer to lactones, ether-linked acrylates, enaminoesters, aromatic esters and beta-diketones needs additional labels.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Linkage-specific labels can prevent a large completion correction from propagating across all ester or multi-carbonyl structures. The selected rows extend this distinction into underconstrained condition ranges.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which of m181, m85, m72, m21 and m26 develop the predicted large weak-eluent response, and which remain closer to the measured modest ester controls?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl response amplitude and shape are scaffold specific. Evidence from aryl ketones and aldehydes supports conditioning transfer on substitution and connectivity; transfer to a ketone with a methylene spacer between its carbonyl and aromatic ring remains an open test.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The observations contain both strong responses and modest controls. Measuring missing branches and transition points should teach structural boundaries for corrections rather than a single carbonyl or polarity offset.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do methoxy, thioether and nitro-substituted carbonyl curves retain distinct shapes, and does m172 remain close to its early baseline at 10/1?

hypotheses.content: Salicylaldehyde-family completion can increase substantially while onset stays relatively early. Whether brominated positional variants preserve this behavior at weak eluent is unresolved. Possible intramolecular hydrogen bonding is a chemical prior, not an established explanation for these labels.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These rows can distinguish learning of completion from onset and test whether a donor-plus-carbonyl representation transfers across substitution patterns and recorded loading contexts.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 50/1, do m197, m186 and m190 retain relatively early onset with broad completion, or do both endpoints rise as predicted?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes reduce the value of repeating several previously targeted regions. m161 at 5/1 had only about 1.00 mL historical completion error in 3774a4dac6dd0f01d48d, and recent m108, m187, m26 and naphthalene controls were mostly close to their acquisition-time predictions. In contrast, m125 in 9bd998a328b109ef639e showed a 21.71 mL completion underprediction, motivating a concrete loading-solvent-volume experiment. Completion misses for m45, m141 and m191 also reinforce endpoint-specific learning without establishing current-model residuals. Earlier structural interpretations require correction: m13 is a multi-carbonyl ester rather than a nitrile; m108 and m116 are aromatic ethers rather than carbonyl scaffolds; m173 is cinnamic acid; and m141 is 2,6-dimethylpyridine. The recent 0/1 and 1/1 naphthalene selections changed both eluent and sample amount, so they do not isolate loading. The present comparisons use stricter matching where available and explicitly retain remaining confounding. No additional labels were revealed during this correction.
batch_rationale: The batch targets relationships that additional labels can resolve. The m125 experiments complete a small factorial design around a recent failure, while m207, m61 and m73 test unusual loading behavior without presuming every discrepancy has a recorded-variable explanation. Constant-loading m208 and m209 pairs challenge large predicted solvent responses in sparsely constrained regions. New m154 measurements and a corresponding m153 weak-eluent control test positional transfer with closely comparable loading. Lactone, aromatic ester, ether-linked acrylate, diketone, acid and aldehyde measurements extend chemical boundaries supported by existing observations, including cases where completion changes independently of onset. Several selections have moderate predicted retention or low CW distance because their matched comparisons are informative. Others test extrapolation because the response relationship is missing, not because large endpoints are intrinsically desirable. Avoiding redundant measurements of recently well-predicted controls leaves capacity to learn structure-condition interactions that recur across the Row-distribution. All 32 rows retain their supplied conditions and premeasurement predictions.
